blocks.content: The Rajya Sabha is a permanent body and not subject to dissolution, whereas the Lok Sabha is not a permanent body and its normal term is five years.

items: An extension of Lok Sabha's tenure during a National Emergency cannot continue beyond a period of six months after the Emergency has ceased to operate.
The power to dissolve the Lok Sabha rests with the President, acting on the advice of the Council of Ministers.
The Constitution itself did not fix the tenure of Rajya Sabha members; it was determined by the Representation of the People Act, 1951.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Lok Sabha is not a permanent body, and its normal term is five years from the date of its first meeting.
The President is authorized to dissolve the Lok Sabha at any time even before the completion of five years.
During a National Emergency, the term of Lok Sabha can be extended by Parliament for one year at a time.
Rajya Sabha is a permanent body and is not subject to dissolution, with one-third of its members retiring every second year.
The Constitution did not fix the tenure of Rajya Sabha members, leaving it to Parliament, which specified six years under the Representation of the People Act, 1951.
